questions.question: What are the three pillars of an effective presentation?
questions.explanation: Effective presentations combine what you say (content), how you say it (delivery) and how you organize it (structure).

questions.question: What is the best practice for presentation slides?
options: Visually clear slides with minimal text that support your spoken message
Slides packed with full paragraphs to read aloud
questions.explanation: Slides should support, not replace, your spoken message — keep text minimal and visuals clear.

questions.question: Which delivery techniques make a presentation engaging?
options: Eye contact, pacing, pausing and vocal variety
Reading the manuscript word for word
Speaking in monotone to seem serious
questions.explanation: Eye contact, varied pace and pitch, and deliberate pauses keep the audience engaged.

questions.question: What helps you manage presentation nerves?
options: Avoiding practice so you stay spontaneous
questions.explanation: Thorough preparation, repeated practice and breathing techniques are the main tools for managing anxiety.

questions.question: What should a good presentation conclusion do?
options: Summarise the main points and end memorably
questions.explanation: A strong conclusion summarises your message and leaves the audience with something memorable.
